summary.what_this_measures: Of the candidates PROVEN wrong by an independent witness, the fraction whose own test suite accepted them anyway. A model that produced one of these answers would be scored as passing a problem it got wrong.
summary.why_unproven_is_discarded: A candidate whose witness does not separate it from the gold solution has not been shown to be wrong. Counting it as a false pass would manufacture the very result this measurement exists to test for, so it is excluded from both denominators and reported separately.
summary.limits: Candidates were written by a model asked to introduce a subtle bug; they are realistic but not a random sample of real model errors. One candidate per item. The witness proves wrongness at a single input, which is sufficient for "wrong" and says nothing about how wrong.

HumanEval/0.bug: uses <= instead of strict <, so a distance exactly equal to the threshold is wrongly reported as close

HumanEval/1.bug: the accumulator `current` is never cleared after a group closes, so each group keeps the text of all previous groups

HumanEval/2.bug: rounds the decimal part to two places, discarding the rest of the fractional digits

HumanEval/3.bug: uses <= 0 instead of < 0, so a balance of exactly zero is reported as below zero

HumanEval/4.bug: divides the summed deviations by n-1 (sample convention) instead of n

HumanEval/5.bug: the guard should be i < len(numbers) - 1, so a delimiter is also appended after the last element

HumanEval/6.bug: records the depth before incrementing on '(', so every group's reported nesting level is one too low

HumanEval/7.bug: matches case-insensitively, so strings that only contain the substring in a different case are wrongly kept

HumanEval/8.bug: the empty-list special case returns product 0 instead of the empty product 1

HumanEval/9.bug: seeds the running maximum with 0 instead of the first element, so all-negative inputs report 0

HumanEval/10.bug: the suffix scan starts at index 1, so a string that is already a palindrome is never detected and gets needlessly extended

HumanEval/11.bug: strips leading zeros from the result, so the returned string is shorter than the inputs when the high bits cancel

HumanEval/12.bug: uses >= so ties keep the last string of maximal length instead of the first

HumanEval/13.bug: the divisor search range excludes min(a, b) itself, so when one number divides the other the answer is too small

HumanEval/14.bug: returns [''] for the empty string instead of an empty list

HumanEval/15.bug: manually appends the final number, producing a leading space when n is 0 and the joined prefix is empty

HumanEval/16.bug: filters to alphabetic characters only, so digits, spaces and punctuation are not counted as distinct characters

HumanEval/17.bug: splits on a literal single space without dropping empty tokens, so an empty input yields [0] instead of []

HumanEval/18.bug: str.count only counts non-overlapping occurrences, but overlapping ones must be counted

HumanEval/19.bug: 'six' and 'seven' are transposed in the word list, so they sort into each other's positions

HumanEval/20.bug: uses <= when updating the best pair, so ties are broken toward the last equally-close pair instead of the first

HumanEval/21.bug: rounds each rescaled value to two decimals, losing precision on values that are not exact hundredths

HumanEval/22.bug: uses type(v) is int instead of isinstance, so booleans (which are ints) are dropped

HumanEval/23.bug: strips surrounding whitespace before counting, so leading and trailing spaces are not counted

HumanEval/24.bug: the descending search starts at n // 2 - 1, skipping n // 2 itself, so even numbers report a divisor that is too small

HumanEval/25.bug: the trial-division loop condition is strict (divisor * divisor < n), so a remaining perfect square of a prime is emitted whole

HumanEval/26.bug: keeps the first occurrence of a repeated value instead of removing every occurrence of values that appear more than once

HumanEval/27.bug: non-alphabetic characters are dropped instead of passed through unchanged

HumanEval/28.bug: strips whitespace from each string before joining, altering the concatenation

HumanEval/29.bug: tests for the prefix anywhere in the string instead of only at position 0

HumanEval/30.bug: uses >= 0, so zero is included among the positive numbers

HumanEval/31.bug: the trial-division range stops before int(sqrt(n)), so squares of odd primes are reported prime

HumanEval/32.bug: never widens the initial [-1, 1] bracket until it contains a sign change, so roots outside that interval are not found

HumanEval/33.bug: excludes index 0 from the set of indices divisible by three, so the first element never takes part in the sort

HumanEval/34.bug: the adjacent-comparison loop stops one element early and never emits the last distinct value

HumanEval/35.bug: initialises the maximum to 0 instead of the first element, so an all-negative list returns 0

HumanEval/36.bug: iterates to n inclusive instead of over integers strictly less than n

HumanEval/37.bug: the write-back range stops at len(l) - 1, so the final even index of an odd-length list keeps its original value

HumanEval/38.bug: applies the same forward rotation as the encoder instead of the inverse rotation

HumanEval/39.bug: the primality test only trial-divides by primes up to 31, so larger composites such as 4181 = 37 * 113 are counted as prime

HumanEval/40.bug: the middle loop starts at i rather than i + 1, so one element can be used twice in the triple

HumanEval/41.bug: counts n-1 opposing cars per car instead of n, returning n*(n-1) rather than n**2

HumanEval/42.bug: the loop starts at index 1, so the first element is never incremented

HumanEval/43.bug: the inner loop starts at i instead of i+1, so a single 0 is paired with itself and reported as a valid pair

HumanEval/44.bug: loop condition is strict (x > base) instead of x >= base, so a value equal to a power of the base emits the base itself as a single digit

HumanEval/45.bug: uses floor division, so any triangle with an odd base*height product loses the .5

HumanEval/46.bug: the DP loop stops at n-1 (range(4, n)) instead of n+1, so it returns fib4(n-1)

HumanEval/47.bug: averages the two middle elements with floor division, truncating the .5 for even-length lists

HumanEval/48.bug: lowercases the text first, so it treats case-differing strings as palindromes

HumanEval/49.bug: the loop runs n-1 times instead of n, computing 2^(n-1) mod p for n >= 1

HumanEval/50.bug: subtracts 5 without wrapping modulo 26, so characters in 'a'..'e' decode past the start of the alphabet

HumanEval/51.bug: only strips lowercase vowels, leaving uppercase A/E/I/O/U in the output

HumanEval/52.bug: rejects only values strictly greater than t, so a value exactly equal to the threshold counts as below it

HumanEval/53.bug: increments x by one y times, so a negative y produces an empty range and x is returned unchanged

HumanEval/54.bug: compares sorted character sequences, so it demands equal multiplicities instead of equal character sets

HumanEval/55.bug: returns the lookahead value b instead of a, so it yields fib(n+1)

HumanEval/56.bug: only checks the final balance and never rejects a negative running depth, so a closing bracket before its opener passes

HumanEval/57.bug: uses strict comparisons, so a list with equal adjacent elements is reported as non-monotonic

HumanEval/58.bug: never de-duplicates, so an element repeated in l1 appears multiple times

HumanEval/60.bug: the range excludes n itself, so the final term is never added

HumanEval/61.bug: only rejects a negative running depth and never checks that the depth returns to zero, so unclosed openers pass

HumanEval/62.bug: keeps the index-0 term, prefixing a spurious leading 0 and shifting every coefficient one place too high

HumanEval/63.bug: the loop runs one iteration short (range(3, n) instead of range(3, n+1)), returning fibfib(n-1)

HumanEval/64.bug: the trailing-y check is case sensitive, so an uppercase 'Y' at the end is not counted

HumanEval/65.bug: rotates the digits left by shift instead of right

HumanEval/66.bug: treats every non-lowercase character as uppercase, so digits, spaces and punctuation are summed too

HumanEval/67.bug: sums individual digit characters rather than parsing whole numbers, so any multi-digit count is wrong

HumanEval/68.bug: uses <= when comparing candidates, so ties are broken toward the largest index instead of the smallest

HumanEval/69.bug: requires frequency strictly greater than the value instead of greater than or equal

HumanEval/70.bug: the two-pointer loop stops at lo < hi, dropping the middle element of any odd-length list

HumanEval/71.bug: the triangle inequality is checked with >= instead of >, so a degenerate triple is accepted and returns area 0.0

HumanEval/72.bug: uses a strict < on the weight, so a sum exactly equal to the maximum weight is rejected

HumanEval/73.bug: the loop bound has a spurious +1, so for even-length arrays one mismatched pair is counted twice

HumanEval/74.bug: the tie is broken toward lst2, but equal totals should return the first list

HumanEval/75.bug: the nested indices force three distinct primes, so products with a repeated prime factor are rejected

HumanEval/76.bug: starts the search at exponent 1 rather than 0, so x == 1 is never recognised as n**0

HumanEval/79.bug: the loop never runs for 0, so zero produces an empty binary body

HumanEval/84.bug: returns bin() output including the '0b' prefix instead of the bare binary string

HumanEval/85.bug: the range stops at len(lst)-1, so the final odd index of an even-length list is skipped

HumanEval/86.bug: uses split() rather than split(' '), collapsing runs of blank spaces

HumanEval/87.bug: reverse=True sorts the rows descending too, when only the columns should be descending

HumanEval/88.bug: the parity test is taken on the already-sorted copy, so it uses min+max instead of the original first+last elements

HumanEval/89.bug: shifts the raw code point without wrapping modulo 26, so letters near the end of the alphabet leave the alphabet

HumanEval/90.bug: does not de-duplicate, so a repeated minimum is returned as the second smallest

HumanEval/91.bug: tests startswith('I') on the sentence rather than checking that the first word is exactly 'I', so words like 'It' count

HumanEval/92.bug: accepts floats with integral value (e.g. 2.0) as integers instead of requiring the int type

HumanEval/93.bug: the vowel test is case-sensitive on the original character, so uppercase vowels are only case-swapped and never shifted

HumanEval/94.bug: the trial-division loop stops before int(sqrt(n)), so perfect squares of primes such as 25 are declared prime

HumanEval/95.bug: uses k == k.lower() instead of k.islower(), so caseless keys such as '123' are treated as lower case

HumanEval/96.bug: iterates to n inclusive, so n itself is included when it is prime instead of only primes strictly less than n

HumanEval/97.bug: operator precedence: the second % 10 applies to the whole product, so the result is the product's unit digit rather than the product of the unit digits

HumanEval/98.bug: the range stops at len(s)-1, so the last even index of an odd-length string is never examined

HumanEval/99.bug: ties are always rounded up with ceil, which is toward zero rather than away from zero for negative values

HumanEval/104.bug: the even-digit set omits '0', so numbers containing a zero are wrongly kept
